title: Owó: Invoicing for Nigerian Small Businesses
summary: A SaaS product with a marketing site, auth screens and an invoicing dashboard, built to learn Next.js layouts and a reusable component library.
body:
Owó (Yoruba for “money”) is invoicing software for Nigerian freelancers and small businesses: send an invoice, get paid, and see who still owes you. It’s a full SaaS product in one codebase, with the website that sells it, the sign-in screens and the app itself. Each part has its own layout, and all of them are built from the same set of components.

**What it does**

- A marketing site with features, pricing in Naira (monthly or yearly), testimonials, an FAQ, a changelog and a contact page.
- A dashboard with revenue, outstanding and overdue totals, a 12-month revenue chart drawn in plain SVG, recent activity, and the overdue invoices to chase.
- Invoices you can filter, search and page through, with the filters kept in the URL. Tapping one opens a quick view over the list, and a direct link or refresh opens the full printable invoice with a WhatsApp share link.
- A new-invoice form with line items, 7.5% VAT and a live total.
- Settings with profile, business, billing and team tabs; a collapsible sidebar that remembers its state; and a drawer on phones.
- A component library page that shows every button, form control, table, dialog and badge in all its states.
- Light and dark mode with no flash on load, and it works down to 360px. All data is sample data, and the sign-in is a demo, not real auth.

**What I learned**

- **Route groups give each part of the product its own layout** without changing the URL. The marketing site, auth screens and app share one root layout and nothing else.
- **Layouts stay mounted; templates don’t.** The sidebar and the settings tab bar keep their state as you move between pages, while the auth pages’ fade-in replays on every visit.
- **Parallel routes let each dashboard panel load and fail on its own,** so one slow chart never holds up the rest.
- **Intercepting routes** turn the same invoice URL into a modal from the list and into a full page on refresh.
- **Composition over boolean props.** Components take children and slots (like a page header’s action buttons) instead of a growing list of on/off settings, and their variants are defined once with class-variance-authority.
- **Keeping data behind one module** (`lib/data.ts`) means the pages won’t change when a real database arrives on Day 16.
